titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in BC Homes: 2026 Costs, Warning Signs & What Vancouver Homeowners Need to Know
titleZh: 卑詩省房屋Poly-B管道更換：2026年成本、警示跡象與溫哥華業主須知
contentEn:
If your Vancouver or Richmond home was built between 1978 and 1998, it may contain polybutylene (Poly-B) piping — a material once celebrated as the future of plumbing, now known to fail without warning. Reno Stars has repiped dozens of BC homes, and this guide covers exactly what to look for, what it costs in 2026, and how to act before a burst pipe turns into a flooded basement.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Does It Matter?

Polybutylene (Poly-B) is a flexible plastic piping system installed in an estimated 3 to 6 million homes across North America between 1978 and 1998. In British Columbia, municipalities including Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and North Vancouver saw widespread adoption during the housing boom of the 1980s.

The pipes themselves are grey, blue, or black plastic tubing typically 1/2" to 1" in diameter, often marked with "PB2110" or "Polybutylene." They were used for the main water supply lines, branch runs to fixtures, and in some cases for radiant in-floor heating systems.

Poly-B fails due to oxidative degradation. The chlorine in municipal water supplies reacts with the pipe's inner wall, causing the material to become brittle, develop micro-fractures, and eventually split or burst. The failure is unpredictable — a pipe that appears fine on inspection can rupture within weeks.

Warning Signs Your Poly-B Pipes Are Failing

Early detection prevents thousands of dollars in water damage. Watch for these indicators:

  • Discoloured or rust-coloured water when you first turn on a tap
  • Reduced water pressure compared to when you moved in
  • Staining on walls, ceilings, or floors near plumbing runs
  • Visible cracks or bulges on exposed pipe sections
  • Pinhole leaks in basement or crawl space plumbing
  • Pipe fitting connections that show white mineral deposits (calcium carbonate buildup from micro-seepage)
  • Unexplained increases in your water bill (a hidden leak)

If you have experienced one pinhole leak, statistical probability strongly suggests additional failures will follow. Insurance companies have taken note: several BC insurers now decline coverage or charge higher premiums for homes with documented Poly-B plumbing.

How Much Does Poly-B Pipe Replacement Cost in BC in 2026?

Full repiping means removing all Poly-B supply lines and replacing them with modern materials — typically copper or cross-linked polyethylene (PEX). The home's layout, size, and accessibility determine final cost.

Home SizeEstimated Cost Range (2026)Timeline
Condo / Townhouse (under 1,000 sq ft)$3,500 – $7,5002 – 4 days
Single-Family Home (1,000 – 2,000 sq ft)$7,500 – $14,0005 – 8 days
Single-Family Home (2,000 – 3,000 sq ft)$12,000 – $20,0008 – 14 days
Heritage / Multi-Level Home (3,000+ sq ft)$18,000 – $35,000+14 – 21 days

Costs include labour, materials (PEX or copper), fixture rerouting, wall repair, and municipal permit fees. Factors that increase cost: homes with crawl spaces (harder access), multi-storey layouts, custom fixture locations, and homes where Poly-B was used for radiant heating as well as supply lines.

The good news: repiping is a capital improvement. Most BC municipalities do not charge HST on plumbing labour for residential upgrades, and the work may qualify for home equity loan financing. Some municipalities offer reduced permit fees for repiping work that includes seismic pipe bracing — ask your contractor.

The Replacement Process: What Happens Day by Day

Reno Stars follows a structured repipe process designed to minimize disruption to your household:

  • Day 1: Permit inspection and water shut-off coordination with your municipality. Plumbers map all existing Poly-B runs using the home's original plans where available.
  • Days 2–5: Removal of accessible Poly-B supply lines. PEX or copper is threaded through wall cavities using minimal invasive openings. Reno Stars uses PEX-A for its flexibility and freeze-resistance — a genuine benefit for Vancouver's occasional winter freeze events.
  • Day 6–7: Connection to all fixtures, faucets, shower valves, and appliance hookups. Pressure testing to 100 PSI to verify every joint and connection.
  • Day 8–10: Wall patching, painting, and trim restoration to match existing finishes. Reno Stars coordinates with professional painters and drywall contractors to return walls to their original condition.
  • Final Inspection: Municipal plumbing inspector reviews the installation. A certificate of completion is issued and filed with the city.

Should You Replace Poly-B Before Selling Your BC Home?

Yes — increasingly, the answer is a firm yes. BC real estate disclosure requirements include known material defects, and Poly-B plumbing must be disclosed. Many buyers' home inspectors specifically flag Poly-B on pre-purchase inspections, and mortgage lenders have begun requiring a plumbing inspection letter for homes built before 1998 in certain Greater Vancouver neighbourhoods.

Buyers who discover Poly-B after closing often renegotiate the purchase price downward by $5,000 to $20,000 — or walk away entirely. Sellers who replace Poly-B before listing typically recover the full cost through a higher sale price and reduced conditional offer periods.

Reno Stars works with BC real estate agents and home inspectors to provide documentation packages for sellers, including video scope inspection of the existing pipes, a written assessment, and a fixed-price repipe quote good for 90 days.

Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Poly-B Failure?

It depends on your insurer and your policy language. Most BC home insurers will cover sudden, accidental water damage from a pipe burst — but they may deny claims if the pipe failure is attributed to gradual deterioration (which Poly-B failures technically are). Some insurers require documentation that the home's plumbing was inspected within the past 12 months.

As of 2025, at least three major BC home insurers have issued guidance bulletins noting Poly-B as a "high-risk plumbing system" and requiring an inspector's letter before renewal. If your insurer has sent you a letter about your plumbing, call Reno Stars before the renewal date — we can often complete an inspection and provide the required documentation within days.

Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, and Across BC

Reno Stars has replaced Poly-B plumbing in homes across Greater Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. Our crews are experienced with the specific challenges of repiping in Vancouver's older housing stock — including homes with brick veneer exteriors, heritage designations, and complex rooflines where supply lines run through difficult-to-access cavities.

We serve homeowners in Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, North Vancouver, West Vancouver, Coquitlam, Surrey, Delta, Langley, Maple Ridge, New Westminster, Port Moody, White Rock, and Port Coquitlam.

Frequently Asked Questions About Poly-B Pipe Replacement

How do I know if my home has Poly-B pipes?

Check the pipes themselves. Poly-B is typically grey, blue-grey, or black flexible plastic piping, usually 1/2" to 1" in diameter. Look where pipes enter the home (near the water meter or main shut-off valve), in the basement ceiling, or at fixture supply connections. Poly-B fittings are often metal (copper or brass) and may show a distinctive grey or white residue. If your home was built or significantly plumbed between 1978 and 1998 and you have not had the plumbing replaced, assume Poly-B until an inspector confirms otherwise.

Is PEX better than copper for repiping?

For most BC homes, PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) is the preferred material. It is freeze-resistant (it expands slightly when water freezes inside it, then returns to shape), requires fewer fittings (reducing potential leak points), and costs 30–40% less than copper. PEX is approved by all BC municipalities and meets the BC Building Code. Copper is still used for exposed fixture connections and in some heritage homes where it is architecturally preferred. Reno Stars uses PEX-A grade materials throughout.

Can I live in my home during repiping?

Yes, with accommodation. The water must be shut off during work hours (typically 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), but service is restored each evening and on weekends. Our crews take care to minimize dust and debris, and we use temporary seals on open wall sections at the end of each workday. Most homeowners are able to remain in the home throughout the project.

How long does a full Poly-B repipe take?

A typical single-family home in Greater Vancouver takes 7 to 14 days from permit approval to final inspection. Condos and townhouses typically complete in 2 to 5 days. Heritage homes and larger properties (3,000+ square feet) may require up to three weeks.

Does repiping add value to my home?

Yes. A documented repipe with municipal certification is a positive selling feature. It removes a material defect disclosure, eliminates a common buyer inspection condition, and — because modern PEX carries a 25-year manufacturer warranty — provides tangible assurance to future buyers. The ROI is typically 80–100% of project cost in increased resale value, plus faster sale cycles.

如果您的溫哥華或列治文房屋建於1978年至1998年之間，裡面可能含有聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道——這種曾被譽為管道未來的材料，如今眾所周知會無預警地破裂。Reno Stars已為卑詩省數十戶家庭進行了管道更換，本文將詳細說明需要留意的事項、2026年的成本，以及如何在爆管導致地下室淹水之前採取行動。

什麼是Poly-B管道？為什麼這很重要？

聚丁烯（Poly-B）是一種柔性塑料管道系統，於1978年至1998年間在北美約三百萬至六百萬戶家庭中使用。在卑詩省，溫哥華、本拿比、列治文及北溫哥華等城市在1980年代的住房熱潮期間廣泛採用這種管道。

這些管道本身為灰色、藍色或黑色塑料管，直徑通常為1/2"至1"，常標有「PB2110」或「Polybutylene」字樣。它們被用於主要供水管線、衛生設備分支管線，在某些情況下也用於輻射地板供暖系統。

Poly-B管道會因氧化降解而失效。自來水中的氯與管道內壁發生反應，導致材料變脆、產生微裂紋，最終斷裂或爆裂。失效是不可預測的——檢查時看似完好的管道可能在數週內破裂。

Poly-B管道失效的警示跡象

及早發現可防止數千元的水災損失。注意以下跡象：

  • 首次打開水龍頭時水色變黃或生銹
  • 與入住時相比水壓下降
  • 管道附近牆壁、天花板或地板出現水漬
  • 外露管道部分可見裂縫或膨脹
  • 地下室或 crawl space 管道出現針孔洩漏
  • 管道配件連接處出現白色礦物質沉積（微滲漏產生的碳酸鈣）
  • 水費莫名增加（有隱藏洩漏）

如果您已經經歷過一次針孔洩漏，統計概率強烈預示更多失效將隨之而來。保險公司已注意到這一點：多家卑詩省保險公司現在拒絕承保或對有Poly-B管道記錄的房屋收取更高保費。

2026年卑詩省Poly-B管道更換費用是多少？

全面更換意味著移除所有Poly-B供水管線並用現代材料替換——通常為銅管或交聯聚乙烯（PEX）。房屋的佈局、面積和可達性決定最終費用。

房屋面積2026年估計費用範圍工期
公寓/聯排別墅（不足1,000平方尺）$3,500 – $7,5002 – 4天
獨立屋（1,000 – 2,000平方尺）$7,500 – $14,0005 – 8天
獨立屋（2,000 – 3,000平方尺）$12,000 – $20,0008 – 14天
Heritage/多層房屋（3,000+平方尺）$18,000 – $35,000+14 – 21天

費用包括人工、材料（PEX或銅管）、衛生設備重新佈線、牆壁修復和市政府許可費。增加成本的因素包括：有 crawl space 的房屋（較難進入）、多層佈局、定製衛生設備位置，以及Poly-B也用於輻射供暖的房屋。

更換流程：每天發生什麼

Reno Stars遵循結構化的更換流程，旨在最大程度減少對家庭的干擾：

  • 第一天：與市政府協調許可檢查和水務關閉。水管工使用房屋原始圖紙（如有）測繪所有現有Poly-B管線。
  • 第2-5天：移除可達的Poly-B供水管線。使用微創开口將PEX或銅管穿過牆腔。Reno Stars使用PEX-A級材料，因其柔韌性和抗凍性——這對於溫哥華偶發的冬季凍融事件是真正的優勢。
  • 第6-7天：連接所有衛生設備、龍頭、淋浴閥和電器接口。進行100 PSI壓力測試以驗證每個接頭和連接。
  • 第8-10天：牆壁修補、噴漆並恢復與現有飾面相匹配的裝飾。Reno Stars與專業油漆工和干牆承包商協調，將牆壁恢復至原始狀態。
  • 最終檢驗：市政府管道檢驗員審查安裝並頒發完成證書。

正在規劃廚房、浴室、全屋或商業裝修？聯絡Reno Stars獲取免費、無義務報價。

出售卑詩省房屋前是否應該更換Poly-B管道？

是的——越來越多情況下答案是肯定的。卑詩省房地產披露要求包括已知材料缺陷，Poly-B管道必須披露。許多買家的房屋檢驗員在購前檢驗中特別標記Poly-B，而抵押貸款機構已開始要求對1998年前建於某些大溫地區的房屋進行管道檢驗信。

買家在過戶後發現Poly-B往往會重新談判 purchase price 下調$5,000至$20,000——或直接放棄。在掛牌前更換Poly-B的賣家通常通過更高的售價和減少有條件要約期限來收回全部成本。

溫哥華、列治文、本拿頭及整個卑詩省的Poly-B管道更換

Reno Stars已在大溫哥華和菲沙河谷各城市的房屋中更換了Poly-B管道。我們的團隊在更換溫哥華老舊房屋管道的具體挑戰方面經驗豐富——包括外牆為磚貼面、有 Heritage 標誌的房屋，以及供水管線穿過難以進入空腔的複雜屋頂線條。

我們服務的業主遍及溫哥華、列治文、本拿比、北溫哥華、西溫哥華、高貴林、薩里、三角洲、蘭里、楓樹嶺、新西敏、滿遜、白石及和高貴林港。

關於Poly-B管道更換的常見問題

如何知道我的房屋是否有Poly-B管道？

檢查管道本身。Poly-B通常為灰色、藍灰色或黑色柔性塑料管，直徑通常為1/2"至1"。查看管道進入房屋的位置（在水錶或主截止閥附近）、地下室天花板或衛生設備供水連接處。Poly-B管件通常為金屬（銅或黃銅），可能顯示灰色或白色殘留物。如果您的房屋建於或進行過重大管道工程1978年至1998年間，且尚未更換管道，應假設存在Poly-B直至檢驗員確認為止。

PEX比銅管更換更好嗎？

對於大多數卑詩省房屋，PEX（交聯聚乙烯）是首選材料。它具有抗凍性（內部水結冰時會輕微膨脹，然後恢復形狀）、需要更少的管件（減少潛在洩漏點），比銅管便宜30-40%。PEX獲得所有卑詩省市政府的批准並符合卑詩省建築規範。銅管仍用於外露衛生設備連接，在某些Heritage房屋中因建築美觀而更受青睞。Reno Stars全程使用PEX-A級材料。

更換期間我可以住在房屋裡嗎？

可以，但需要配合。更換期間工作時間（通常為上午8:00至下午5:00）必須關閉水務，但每天晚上和周末都會恢復供水。我們的工作人員會盡量減少灰塵和碎屑，並在每個工作日結束時對開放的牆壁部分使用臨時密封件。大多數業主能夠在整個項目期間留在房屋內。

全面的Poly-B更換需要多長時間？

大溫哥華地區的典型獨立屋從許可批准到最終檢驗需要7至14天。公寓和聯排別墅通常在2至5天內完成。Heritage房屋和較大房屋（3,000+平方尺）可能需要最多三週。

更換管道會增加房屋價值嗎？

是的。有市政府認證的更換管道記錄是一個積極的銷售亮點。它消除了一個材料缺陷披露，消除了常見的買家檢驗條件，並且——因為現代PEX帶有25年製造商保修——為未來買家提供了切實的保障。投資回報率通常為項目成本的80-100%，加上更快的銷售週期。
